source_caption:
🎬 Hotel Rwanda (2004)

Hotel Rwanda tells the powerful true story of Paul Rusesabagina, a hotel manager whose courage and determination become a source of hope during one of the darkest chapters in modern history. Set in Rwanda during the 1994 genocide, the film follows Paul as escalating tensions between Hutu extremists and the Tutsi population erupt into widespread violence. Working at the luxurious Hôtel des Mille Collines in Kigali, Paul initially focuses on protecting his wife, Tatiana, and their children as the country descends into chaos. However, as thousands of innocent civilians face unimaginable danger, he transforms the hotel into a refuge for desperate families seeking safety. Using his diplomatic skills, personal connections, and extraordinary resourcefulness, Paul negotiates with military officials, government representatives, and international contacts in an attempt to protect those sheltering inside. With limited supplies, constant threats, and little outside assistance, every decision becomes a matter of life and death. As the violence intensifies, Paul must confront the terrifying reality of international inaction while struggling to maintain hope for the people depending on him. Through heartbreaking moments, extraordinary acts of compassion, and overwhelming uncertainty, the film reveals the devastating human consequences of hatred and political conflict. Featuring powerful performances and deeply emotional storytelling, Hotel Rwanda explores courage, sacrifice, humanity, family, survival, and the extraordinary difference one person can make when standing against injustice.

🎭 Genre: Biography • Drama • History • War

⭐ IMDb: 8.1/10

⏱️ Runtime: 2h 1m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Terry George

✍️ Writers: Keir Pearson & Terry George

source_details.synopsis: Hotel Rwanda is a 2004 biographical historical drama film co-written and directed by Terry George. It was adapted from a screenplay by George and Keir Pearson, and stars Don Cheadle and Sophie Okonedo as hotelier Paul Rusesabagina and his wife Tatiana. The film depicts Rusesabagina's efforts to save the lives of his family and more than 1,500 other refugees by providing them with shelter in the besieged Hôtel des Mille Collines during the Rwandan genocide, which occurred during the spring of 1994.
